title.title: A 3-manifold without conjugate points or nonpositive curvature
title.subtitle: Claim: a closed 3-manifold has a metric whose geodesics never refocus, but no metric with $\sec \le 0$

plain: A space where straight paths never meet again, though it can't be curved like a saddle everywhere

beats.text: Closed 3-manifolds, schematically. Nonpositive curvature implies no conjugate points
Asked: does every manifold on the left also admit nonpositive curvature?
No: Leeb's graph manifold carries a metric whose geodesics never refocus

steps: Take a graph manifold that Leeb showed has no nonpositive curvature
Put a carefully built metric on it
Its geodesics never refocus anyway: no conjugate points

achievement.label: Question of Ivanov–Kapovitch (2014) and Burns–Matveev
statement: \exists\, M^3 \text{ closed, with no conjugate points,}
achievement.context: Leeb (1995) ruled out $\sec \le 0$; the new part is the metric without conjugate points
achievement.note: It also has no metric without focal points

voice.text: Nonpositive curvature stops geodesics refocusing. Is the converse true for closed manifolds?
Leeb's graph manifold gets a careful metric whose geodesics never refocus at all.
Claimed: no, the converse fails in dimension three.

sources.quote: with a smooth metric without conjugate points but no metric of nonpositive sectional curvature
and no metric without focal points
